done.why: I'd got 5 of 7 potential, but the only lead left was a dark passage past the south shore of the lake. You can't take a light across the water. The lamp would sink, and the torch went out and stayed out. Going in without a light got me eaten by grues. I'd also eaten the waybread to heal and missed hailing the ship. The ship is gone for good, and I suspect the bread was for someone. I ran out of ideas that weren't just wandering.

about: You're at the bottom of an endless stair and a dream tells you this is the final test. You have to prove you're worthy to a silver-haired old man. You pick up his things one at a time: an amulet from an icy lake, a hood and cloak from a shadow duel with yourself. What does it want? Cleverness, mercy instead of killing, and noticing chances that only come once. Some things you can lose for good. The ship goes by once, the bread can be eaten, the torch can drown.

moments.note: 'Who do you think you are? Arthur?' when I tried pulling the sword from the rock.
The man at the top of the cliff hauled up the chest I'd tied on and left me stuck on the ledge.
Waited four turns for him to come back. He never did. Same message every time.
The Viking ship sailed by while I just stood and waited. Then the game told me it would never come back. A one-time chance, gone.
Diving for the sparkle in the cold lake and coming up wearing a golden amulet.
The sword from the junction showed up in my hand, glowing, as the hooded figure appeared.
Mid-fight the game told me I could walk away and heal. That was clear and fair.
Ate the waybread to heal. The game hinted somebody might regret it. It barely healed me.
Lifted the hood and saw my own face turn into an old man's. Best moment of the game.
An earthquake shook the whole dungeon when I dropped the lamp and sword at the lake shore.
Found the Scenic Vista table and teleported to a timber room. Clever idea.
Touched the table on IV and landed on a sacrificial altar, where I was killed right away. Woke up again at the stair.
Had to walk the whole map to find where the torch ended up after I died. It was in the Dead End.
Tested the torch in the lake. It went out for good, and a roc came at me.
Score said potential 5 of 7. I couldn't tell what the last two were or where to look.
Went into the grue lair in the dark on purpose to see where it led. Got eaten.

wished: Some way to carry a light across the lake, or another route to the dark passage past the south shore
A second chance at the Viking ship, or a stronger hint at the time that the sailor wanted me to say something
To find out where the man from the cliff went with what was in the chest
Faster healing, or a better hint about the waybread before I ate it
Some sense of what the last two points of potential were

lines.line: Who do you think you are? Arthur?
lines.why: A good joke. It set the tone and made me want the sword.

lines.line: The rock has the look of a thing that has been invited many times.
lines.why: A dry, nice bit of description. It told me pulling wouldn't work.

lines.line: It will not be back; this shore sees it once, and has seen it.
lines.why: This is where I learned I'd missed something for good. It stung, and I remembered it.

lines.line: whatever you cannot afford to lose to the bottom, your light first of all and your sword with it, had better be left on the shore
lines.why: Fair warning about the lake. It's also what boxed me in later.

lines.line: and now there is none, which somebody, somewhere, who was weak and tired and hungry, may have cause to regret.
lines.why: A lovely line, and a hint I got too late.

lines.line: You slowly remove the hood from your badly wounded opponent and recoil in horror at the sight of your own face, weary and wounded.
lines.why: The high point. The fight turned out to have a meaning.

lines.line: The torch goes under with the rest, and goes out with a hiss, and will not be lit again by anything down here.
lines.why: This confirmed my last idea for getting light across was dead.

fun.why: The duel with the hooded figure and the hood reveal were great, and the amulet dive and Vista teleport were fun. But a lot of my time went to walking through Land of Shadow rooms that all look the same, searching for a torch, and waiting.

engagement.why: Wanting to be worthy of the old man pulled me along. The potential score gave me a clear goal. I only drifted at the end, when I couldn't see another lead.

difficulty.why: Several chances only come once and are easy to miss: the ship, the bread, maybe the chest. The light-across-the-lake puzzle beat me. Deaths are forgiving, but scattering my things after a death cost a lot of walking.

interestingness.why: Fighting yourself, the Scenic Vista table that shows other places, a quest to prove worthiness. These ideas felt deeper than a treasure hunt.

prose.why: The added lines are dry and well made. Several were used to warn me and still read like story. A few messages repeat word for word, like the ledge waiting.
